Welcome to King Ina C of E Academy
LET YOUR LIGHT SHINE
Within our secure Christian environment, our vision is to develop healthy, happy, motivated learners who aspire to achieve their full potential and who look to the future with confidence.
A very warm welcome to King Ina Church of England Academy. Our school is set within beautiful countryside on the edge of the rural town of Somerton. We have provision for 14 primary classes in addition to our pre-school. Our site includes a large sports field, Forest School, an adventure playground and a multi-use games area. We have an incredibly dedicated team of staff at King Ina who are committed to helping the children achieve their very best and to ensuring that the pupils’ well-being is at the centre of all we do. OPAL play, a school therapy dog and our bespoke nurture provision are all integral to supporting the children’s mental health and well-being. Pupils take on many and varied leadership roles within the school including School Council, Ethos Team, Eco Council, Peer Mediators, Sport Captains and House Captains. Our Christian values of Friendship, Perseverance, Service, Respect, Trust and Compassion are central to the children’s learning.
Thank you for taking time to look at our website. We warmly welcome visits to our school and appointments can be made by contacting the school office by telephone on 01458 272587 or via email on: office@kingina.co.uk

SIAMS (church school inspection)
Friday 24th April 2026
Dear Parents and Carers,
We are delighted to share with you the outcome of our recent SIAMS (Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools) inspection. We are incredibly proud of the report, which recognises the many strengths of our school community and reflects the hard work, care and commitment shown by our children, staff and families every day.
The inspection highlights that King Ina Church of England Academy “is living up to its foundation as a Church school and is enabling pupils and adults to flourish.” This reflects our shared vision:
“Let your light shine” (Matthew 5:14–16)
Inspectors recognised that our vision is truly at the heart of everything we do, noting leaders’ “unwavering commitment to the Christian vision… [which] shapes the school’s character and daily practice.” They also highlighted our “culture of compassion and support” where “pupils and adults thrive.” In addition, collective worship was praised as “thoughtfully and effectively structured,” enabling pupils to reflect deeply and grow spiritually.
The report also specifically recognises the impact of leadership, noting the “wholehearted commitment demonstrated by leaders… to living the vision [which] enables pupils and adults to flourish.” This highlights the dedication of our leaders in ensuring that every decision is rooted in what is best for the children and the whole school community.
These comments show what a caring, supportive and aspirational environment our school is, and how well our children and staff work together to live out these values each day. Overall, the report celebrates our school as a place where children are happy, work hard and support one another, enabling everyone to flourish.
As with any inspection, there are also areas identified for development. We welcome these next steps and are already working on how we can build on our strong foundations.
Thank you for your continued support and for playing such an important role in making our school such a special place where every child can truly “let their light shine.”

Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
King Ina C of E Academy is an inclusive school where ALL pupils, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), are supported to achieve their full potential within a secure Christian environment.
The school follows Somerset’s Graduated Response Tool to identify barriers to learning and implement appropriate strategies. Provision is in line with the SEND Code of Practice (2014), meaning pupils may receive support that is different from or additional to that normally available.
Identification and Support
Early identification of needs is prioritised.
The school works with parents to agree strengths, needs, targets, and provisions.
A structured Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR) cycle is followed.
External professionals are involved where necessary.
Mrs Jodie Stock (Mon–Wed)
Mrs Laura Ruddle (Tue–Thu)
Mrs Clare Horsey (Owlets Nursery)
SENCos collaborate closely with each other and the Senior Leadership Team.
Parents should speak with their child’s class teacher first, and then arrange an appointment with a SENCo if needed.
SEND Information Report
Further details on identification, assessment, and provision are set out in the school’s SEND Information Report, available via the school.

Maths at King Ina Academy
Our vision for mathematics
At King Ina Academy, we want every child to become a confident mathematician who understands the mathematics they are learning, can explain their thinking and can use their knowledge to solve problems.
We believe that all children can succeed in mathematics. Our maths curriculum focuses on developing fluency, reasoning and problem solving, while building the secure knowledge and skills children need for future learning.
We want maths to be engaging, purposeful and enjoyable, with children encouraged to explore ideas, make connections, talk about their thinking and develop their confidence as mathematicians.
Our approach to maths
We use White Rose Maths as the foundation for our mathematics curriculum. Our teachers use this carefully planned progression alongside their own professional judgement, adapting lessons and activities to meet the needs of the children in their class. This ensures that all children are appropriately supported, challenged and encouraged to develop a deep and lasting understanding of mathematics. White Rose Maths is built around three key areas: fluency, reasoning and problem solving, which work together to develop confident and capable mathematicians.
Children develop secure knowledge of number facts, calculation methods and mathematical vocabulary.
Reasoning
Children explain how and why they have reached an answer and learn to justify their thinking.
Problem solving
Children apply their mathematical knowledge to different situations and unfamiliar problems.
